_comment: MAILGATEHTTPAPI1027: shared cases of the HTTP mail API rule in both mail gates (scripts/hooks/outgoing-copy-gate.py :: _mail_api_sends, scripts/email-send-gate.mjs :: mailApiSends). Each body is written to a script file and judged by script_run_sends / scriptRunSends, and passed as a -c / -e code string to is_send_invocation / isSendInvocation; both twins must answer `expected` on both paths. Origin: Marveen 50920, a Gmail REST send from a python script file passed the main agent's approval gate. A case may carry `helpers` (file name -> body): local modules written next to it, so the one-level helper read is pinned too; such a case is judged as a script file only, since a code string has no helper of its own here. MAILGATEHEREDOCFP1027: a send marker in a docstring, a comment or a prose literal is no send (the prose-literal masker). A case with `file_only` is judged as a script file only: the code-string path's older exec heuristic (an exec word and a sender word anywhere, pinned by send-invocation-cases.json) stays looser on purpose.

inline_comment: MAILCURLSEND1118: an HTTP mail API send written inline on the command line (curl, wget, httpie, xh) is judged like the same send in a script. Each `inline` cmd runs through is_send_invocation / isSendInvocation in both twins' tests (scripts/__tests__/mail-api-send-cases.test.py, src/__tests__/mail-api-send-cases.test.ts). On a literal mail-only API host (normalised host and path) only a known read passes (GET or HEAD without a body on that provider's API path); Graph, which is not mail-only, sends on its send paths; a host that is not literal is decided by the provider send paths (or a mail API host elsewhere in the line), a send unless a plain read. The boundary is written out at _inline_mail_api_sends in outgoing-copy-gate.py.

url_file_comment: MAILURLFILE1118: a request whose URL (and method, headers, body) comes from a FILE the line only names: a curl config file (-K / --config) or a wget input file (-i / --input-file). Each `url_file` case writes its `files` (relative path -> text) into a fresh directory, replaces `{dir}` in `cmd` with it, and runs `cmd` through is_send_invocation / isSendInvocation with that directory as the cwd, in both twins' tests. `class` names the shape: `send` (the file is read and the request is a mail send), `allow` (the file is read and it is none), `undecidable` (the file cannot be read here: a send only when the line carries a mail marker, a mail-only API host or a Microsoft Graph host, the file's text included). The rows of `inline` named for a method-override header, a national cloud or an unparseable command belong to the same follow-up. The boundary is written out at _url_file_words in outgoing-copy-gate.py.
